name: Odd Figure Out
shortcutSummary: Compare all figures for a common property: number of sides, open vs closed, number of internal elements, shading, rotation pattern, or symmetry. The odd one lacks this property.
conceptExplanation: Odd Figure Out questions show 4-5 figures, and you must identify the one that doesn't belong. The common property could be structural (number of lines/curves), orientational (rotation), or compositional (number/type of internal elements).

subtopics.name: Odd Figure Out — Core Concepts
subtopics.explanation: Odd Figure Out questions show 4-5 figures, and you must identify the one that doesn't belong. The common property could be structural (number of lines/curves), orientational (rotation), or compositional (number/type of internal elements).
shortcuts: Count Elements: Count lines, curves, dots, or enclosed regions in each figure.
Symmetry Check: Most figures may have line/rotational symmetry while one doesn't.
Open vs Closed: Check if all but one figure is a closed shape (or vice versa).

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Out of the four given figures A, B, C, and D, three are similar in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd figure out:

Figures A, B, and C are closed polygons (Triangle, Rectangle, Pentagon), whereas Figure D is an open spiral curve.
practiceQuestions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C are closed geometric polygons composed of straight line segments, whereas Figure D is an open non-closed curve.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (open curve).

practiceQuestions.questionText:
Out of the four given figures A, B, C, and D, three are similar in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd figure out:

Figures A, B, and C possess bilateral line symmetry (can be divided into two identical halves by a line), whereas Figure D is completely asymmetrical.
practiceQuestions.hint: Check structural properties: closed vs open, number of sides (odd/even), symmetry, or rotational sense.
practiceQuestions.explanation: Figures A, B, and C have at least one line of symmetry, whereas Figure D lacks any line of symmetry.
practiceQuestions.solutionSteps:
Step 1: Check basic properties: number of straight lines, closed vs open contours.
Step 2: Check symmetry and rotational direction.
Step 3: The odd figure that does not conform to the group rule is Figure D (asymmetrical figure).
